setup.title: Setup
setup.sub: Everything XENO STORE needs to install games with one tap, checked on this console.
setup.checklistHint: Each check explains the fix. Optional items are nice to have.
setup.payloadManager: Add XENO STORE to Payload Manager
setup.payloadManagerHint: Source URL and QR for the Payload Manager app, so updates arrive automatically
setup.ghostCleanerHint: Folders under /data/homebrew that ShadowMountPlus turns into home-screen icons
setup.allOk: {n, plural, one{# check passed} other{All # checks passed}}

explain.shadowmount: ShadowMountPlus mounts exFAT/FFPFSC images from homebrew/ and shows them on the home screen. XENO STORE asks it to rescan after an image download; it never replaces it.
explain.dpi: A package installer daemon on 127.0.0.1:9040 lets XENO STORE install PKGs when the direct AppInstUtil call is refused on this firmware.
explain.etahen: etaHEN's installer on 127.0.0.1:12800 is the second fallback for PKG installs.
explain.internet: A HEAD request to the catalog revision URL. Without internet the saved catalog still works; downloads need the network.
explain.drive: The default download drive must be writable: XENO STORE creates and removes a small test file there.
explain.space: Keep a few GB free on the default drive; the queue refuses files that do not fit.
explain.firmware: Shows the console firmware. FPKG installs depend on the exploit chain of your firmware.
explain.payload-manager: With Payload Manager auto-start, XENO STORE loads on every boot and updates itself from the XENOKING feed.

setup.pmText: Scan the code on your phone or open the URL, then add it as a source in Payload Manager (itsPLK). XENO STORE and its updates appear in its list.
setup.pmStep1: Open Payload Manager on the console and choose Add source.
setup.pmStep2: Enter the URL above (or paste it from your phone after scanning the QR).
setup.pmStep3: Pick XENO STORE in the list, send it, and optionally enable auto-start.
setup.ghostLoadFailed: The homebrew folder could not be listed
setup.ghostNote: ShadowMountPlus registers every folder here as a home-screen icon; deleting a folder removes its icon on the next scan.
setup.ghostEmptyHint: Nothing under /data/homebrew yet — nothing can leave a ghost icon.
setup.ghostDeleteText: The folder {name} ({size}) and everything inside it will be deleted from /data/homebrew. Its home-screen icon disappears after the next ShadowMountPlus scan.
setup.ghostDeleteSelf: This is XENO STORE's own home-screen app — the store keeps running until you stop it, but the icon is gone.
setup.ghostDeleteSure: Really delete {name}? This cannot be undone.
setup.ghostDeletedHint: Run a ShadowMountPlus scan to refresh the home screen
setup.nudgeText: A quick check tells you what to install for one-tap game installs.

accounts.intro: Offline activation writes an account id into a profile's registry slot so games and saves work without PSN. Proven by ps5-payload-dev's offact; reboot afterwards.

accounts.warn2: A reboot is required afterwards. Do it on a secondary profile if you are unsure.
accounts.warn3: The id is derived from the profile name unless you enter your own (for example the one from a previous activation).

accounts.clearText: The account id in the registry slot is reset. Games tied to it may ask to sign in again. Reboot afterwards.
accounts.fakeText: np-fake-signin.elf pretends PSN is signed in so trophies pop offline; np-fake-signout.elf reverts it. Both come from the companion catalog (earthonion/np-fake-signin), are checked against their SHA-256 and sent to the ELF loader on :9021.
accounts.fakeMissing: The companion feed lists no fake sign-in payloads right now.
accounts.fakeNote: Activate the profile first; the fake sign-in does nothing on a profile without an account id.
